query: The Old Schoolmistress {In the market you're stopped by the old schoolmistress who taught half the town its letters. "Come and tell my little ones about the academy," she says. "They won't believe me."|The schoolmistress again, with her satchel of slates. "They've talked of nothing else since last time. Come back."|The schoolmistress waves from across the square. The children at her heels are wearing paper wizard hats, badly folded.} {She looks smaller than she used to.|She smells of chalk, as she always did.|{season == "winter": Her breath steams; she's been out in the cold looking for you.|A market dog is following her for the biscuits in her pocket.}} Visit the schoolroom {You tell twenty children about the moving stairs and the floating candles. One asks if you've met a dragon. You lie a little. They swarm you like bees.|You show them a single small flame in your palm. Twenty faces light up. You're exhausted after an hour, the good way.|You answer questions until your voice gives out. One of them wants to go to the academy now, very badly. It's your fault, and you're glad.} Buy her tea and listen {You buy her a pot of tea and she tells you which of your old classmates married whom, and which ran off to sea. You'd forgotten you missed them.|She asks what you're studying and actually listens. Then she corrects your grammar, out of habit, and you let her.|You buy her tea and she tells you what you were like at seven. It's alarming how little you've changed.}
